trick: Lint and typecheck after every edit, or once at the end?
source_note: Season 2 lineup (19 Oct, Speed; was day 46 in the 15 Sep plan; module 5 tier-list Short). Same check script on both sides (.claude/hooks/lint-check.py, byte-identical copies, checked with cmp): ESLint with the repo's own config (errors only) on changed JavaScript files and tsc --noEmit on the package of a changed TypeScript file. Only the hook event differs. With: PostToolUse on Edit|Write|MultiEdit checks the file just edited and shows its errors to the agent (exit 2). Without: Stop checks every file changed since HEAD when the agent tries to finish and blocks with the errors, at most 8 times (Claude Code's cap; enforced in the script too, as on day 43). No CLAUDE.md or prompt change on either side. Baseline measured 23 Oct on a clone: tsc clean for frai-cli, frai-gate and frai-agent; ESLint errors only in frai-core key-store.js, documents/helpers.js and providers/openai.js (one unused variable each) plus two built dist files, which no hook checks. Both hooks report the pre-existing error if the agent changes one of those three files (the h3 reference fix changes key-store.js and leaves it; on the without side that alone uses all 8 Stop blocks unless the agent fixes it). Standard verdict rule. Pre-registered count (check_lint.py, in each row's extra): errors the agent added that are still there at the end ('new': lint errors in changed files minus the same files' errors at lab-base, plus type errors), and minutes per run; hook runs, hook reports and seconds spent in the hook are recorded too.
